keyFacts.label: Non-resident foreigners who entered Colombia for health reasons in 2025, up 18.4% on 2024 (Migración Colombia data published by Bogotá's tourism institute). Jan to Aug 2026: 21,034, up 17.6%.
Share of health-motivated foreign visitors who came from the United States, the largest single market, followed by the Netherlands (18%) and Panama (7%), per the travel-agency association Anato.

Hospitals and clinics shown as holding Icontec national accreditation, the only Colombian accreditation body, out of thousands of licensed providers. Four to six hold Joint Commission International accreditation.

Deaths after cosmetic procedures in Medellín in 2024, 2025 and 2026 to May, per Antioquia's health secretary, who also reported 379 complications and 64 aesthetic centres closed in two years. Colombia keeps no national registry of these deaths.

treatmentsIntro: Colombia's international patients split into two very different streams. One is cosmetic surgery sold on price and volume in Cali, Medellín, Bogotá and Barranquilla, where ISAPS counted 490,944 aesthetic procedures in 2024 and about 30% of surgical patients were foreign. The other is dental, cardiac, orthopedic, fertility and eye care at a small set of accredited hospitals, which is where most of Medellín's 23,323 recorded international patients in 2024 actually went: 59% came for diagnostics and 14% for ophthalmology, against 10% for plastic surgery.

treatments.name: Plastic and cosmetic surgery (BBL, liposuction, breast, rhinoplasty, facelift, 'mommy makeover')
treatments.whyHere: Concentrated in Cali, Medellín, Bogotá and Barranquilla. Colombia has roughly 960 plastic surgeons, a deep private-clinic market and prices that marketplaces put at 60% to 75% below US surgeon fees. ISAPS ranked Colombia second only to Thailand for foreign plastic-surgery patients in 2018 and reported about 30% of 2024 surgical patients came from abroad, led by the US, Spain and Canada. The same market also hosts the clandestine 'clínicas de garaje' and combined-procedure packages behind most of the documented deaths.
treatments.demand: ISAPS 2024: 490,944 aesthetic procedures in Colombia; liposuction 41,280, breast augmentation 33,984, blepharoplasty 28,032. Medellín: plastic surgery was 10% of international-patient services in 2024. Cali recorded 3,331 health visitors in Jan to May 2024, 1,752 of them from the US.
treatments.typicalStay: 10 to 14 days for body contouring; 7 to 10 days for facial work. CDC advises not flying for 10 days after abdominal or chest surgery.

treatments.name: Dental (implants, All-on-4, veneers, smile design)
treatments.whyHere: Bogotá, Medellín and Cali. The Sociedad Colombiana de Odontología told La República that 20% to 40% of aesthetic-dentistry patients are foreign. Marketplaces list single implants at US$700 to US$1,500 against US$3,000 to US$5,000 in the US. Implant work needs two trips several months apart unless an immediate-load protocol is used.
treatments.demand: No official national count. Bogotá's tourism institute lists dentistry among the top specialties for its 7,320 health visitors in Jan to Aug 2026.
treatments.typicalStay: 5 to 7 days per trip; implants usually need a second trip 3 to 6 months later.

treatments.name: Bariatric surgery (gastric sleeve, bypass)
treatments.whyHere: Bogotá, Cali and Medellín hospitals. Bogotá's tourism institute lists bariatric surgery among its medical-tourism specialties. Marketplace ranges are US$4,500 to US$7,000 for a sleeve against US$15,000 to US$25,000 self-pay in the US. ASMBS defines bariatric travel as any distance that prevents routine follow-up and warns that continuity of care is the core problem.
treatments.typicalStay: 7 to 10 days; CDC advises no flying for 10 days after abdominal surgery.

treatments.name: Hair transplant (FUE)
treatments.whyHere: Medellín and Bogotá clinics market FUE heavily to US men, often bundled with other cosmetic work. No official demand figure exists and no clinic-published 2025 to 2026 price could be sourced in this research; marketplaces quote low thousands of dollars per 2,000 grafts but could not be pinned to a dated page. Treat all hair-transplant pricing as unverified until a clinic quotes in writing.

treatments.name: Stem cell and 'regenerative' therapy
treatments.whyHere: Medellín is the hub, led by US-owned BioXcellerator and smaller clinics. Status: Colombia has no official authorization for stem cell treatments outside clinical trials except established blood-disorder uses; INVIMA has approved specific trials (for example a 2020 BioXcellerator and Clínica Somer COVID trial) but the only INVIMA material on general advanced-therapy rules is a 2017 framework presentation. In July 2026 Supersalud and the Fiscalía raided Bogotá sites that advertised 'stem cells' to Mexican and Costa Rican patients and were actually injecting biopolymers, which Ley 2316 de 2023 bans. These treatments are not FDA approved.

treatments.name: Fertility (IVF)
treatments.whyHere: Bogotá and Medellín. Bogotá's tourism institute lists fertility among its leading specialties. The only dated comparative price found is a 2021 Medical Tourism Association table: US$5,450 per cycle in Colombia versus US$12,400 in the US.
treatments.typicalStay: Two trips or one stay of 2 to 3 weeks around stimulation and transfer.

treatments.name: Cardiac, orthopedic and oncology care at accredited hospitals
treatments.whyHere: Bogotá (Fundación Cardioinfantil-LaCardio, Fundación Santa Fe), Medellín (Hospital Pablo Tobón Uribe, JCI since 2015, re-accredited October 2021) and Cali (Fundación Valle del Lili, which states JCI accreditation). Bogotá's tourism institute lists cardiology and oncology among its top specialties. Marketplace tables put knee replacement at US$7,000 to US$12,500 and a 2021 table put heart bypass at US$14,800.
treatments.demand: No procedure-level official figure. Medellín's cluster reported 59% of 2024 international-patient services were diagnostics and 5% executive check-ups.
treatments.typicalStay: 10 to 21 days for joint replacement; longer for cardiac surgery.

treatments.name: Ophthalmology and dermatology
treatments.whyHere: Medellín, where ophthalmology was 14% of international-patient services in 2024, and Bogotá, which lists ophthalmology among its leading specialties. LASIK was quoted at US$2,400 in Colombia versus US$4,000 in the US in the 2021 MTA table.

howItWorks.title: Who regulates what
howItWorks.body: The Ministerio de Salud sets the licensing standard (habilitación, Resolución 3100 de 2019); departmental and district health secretariats inspect, license and seal providers; the Superintendencia Nacional de Salud (Supersalud) supervises and receives complaints; INVIMA regulates drugs, devices and biologics; Medicina Legal performs autopsies; the Fiscalía prosecutes. Colombia has no national registry of cosmetic-surgery deaths, and Medicina Legal's last published count dates from 2016 (36 deaths).

howItWorks.title: Lookup 1: REPS, is the clinic licensed for surgery?
howItWorks.body: Every legal provider is in the Registro Especial de Prestadores de Servicios de Salud. Go to prestadores.minsalud.gov.co/habilitacion, open the current REPS module, click 'Registro Actual', then search by 'Prestador' (provider), 'Sedes' (sites), 'Servicios' and 'Capacidad instalada'. The key check for cosmetic surgery: the exact site where you will be operated must list the service 'cirugía plástica y estética' and a licensed operating room (sala de cirugía) under installed capacity. A provider licensed only for 'consulta externa' or 'medicina estética' may not operate. In the August 2026 Bogotá bichectomía death the site was licensed only for outpatient consultation.

howItWorks.title: Lookup 2: ReTHUS, is the doctor a registered specialist?
howItWorks.body: The Registro Único Nacional del Talento Humano en Salud is the national licence register. On the SISPRO ReTHUS page enter the clinician's full name or cédula number and profession; the result shows profession, authorization status, the entity that registered them and any ethical-disciplinary sanctions. The Ministry has stated that practicing a medical-surgical specialty that is not recorded in ReTHUS is illegal practice, so check that 'cirugía plástica, estética y reconstructiva' appears as the registered specialty, not just 'medicina'. The lookup is free.

howItWorks.title: Lookup 3: SCCP directory, and why 'esteticista' is not a surgeon
howItWorks.body: The Sociedad Colombiana de Cirugía Plástica, Estética y Reconstructiva lists its members at cirugiaplastica.org.co/buscar-cirujano. Colombia recognises one surgical specialty for this work, 'cirugía plástica, estética y reconstructiva'; 'medicina estética' and 'cirugía estética' are not recognised specialties and much of that training is short courses, per the Ministry of Education. General physicians, dentists and non-clinicians have performed liposuction and gluteal fat grafting in several fatal cases. Ley 1799 de 2016 bans cosmetic procedures on minors. A bill to restrict operating to postgraduate-trained specialists in licensed facilities (PL 311/2023 Cámara, 237/2024 Senado) was still pending in 2025 and the SCCP says at least five such bills have died in Congress.

howItWorks.title: Accreditation versus 'rankings'
howItWorks.body: Icontec is Colombia's sole accreditation body and lists accredited institutions at acreditacionensalud.org.co/instituciones; 64 were displayed in October 2026. Joint Commission International accreditation is held by a handful: Hospital Pablo Tobón Uribe (Medellín, since 2015, re-accredited 2021), Fundación Valle del Lili (Cali, states JCI on its site), and Fundación Cardioinfantil and Fundación Santa Fe in Bogotá are widely reported as JCI accredited; confirm current status in JCI's own directory because hospital pages did not show dates. Lists such as 'top 20 clinics in Latin America' are magazine rankings (IntelLat, América Economía), not accreditation. Stand-alone cosmetic clinics are almost never accredited; for them REPS licensing is the check.

howItWorks.title: What US agencies and societies have said
howItWorks.body: The CDC Yellow Book tells medical tourists to verify international accreditation and board-equivalent certification, obtain English records before leaving, and not fly for 10 days after chest or abdominal surgery or 7 to 10 days after facial procedures. A CDC study published June 2026 reviewed US residents harmed after travel for cosmetic procedures in 2014 to 2024: 21 consultations, about 145 patients, four involving deaths, with nontuberculous mycobacteria the leading pathogen and liposuction and abdominoplasty the leading procedures. ASPS warns that patients injured abroad have little legal recourse and that complications are often paid for by Medicaid or the patient. The State Department rates Colombia Level 3, Reconsider Travel.

howItWorks.title: Facilitators, 'coordinators' and recovery houses
howItWorks.body: Much foreign cosmetic demand is sold by intermediaries who package surgery, hotel and transport, often as multi-procedure 'combos'. Antioquia's health secretary said in 2021 that hotels were 'lending themselves' to these packages; the Personería de Medellín found 11 post-op patients in one hotel and warned recovery lodging is unregulated. A coordinator is not a licensed provider, appears nowhere in REPS, and cannot be held to the clinic's duty of care. Pay the licensed clinic directly and confirm which named surgeon will operate.

howItWorks.title: Recourse, insurance and HSAs
howItWorks.body: In Colombia a patient can file a free PQRD complaint with Supersalud via the SuperArgo portal, report to the local health secretariat (which can seal the clinic), file a criminal complaint with the Fiscalía, and bring an ethics complaint to the Tribunal de Ética Médica, which has suspended surgeons. Civil damages require a Colombian lawyer and years. US courts rarely have jurisdiction over Colombian doctors, per ASPS. US health plans generally exclude cosmetic surgery and its complications. IRS Publication 502 does not restrict deductible care by country, but cosmetic surgery is not deductible unless it corrects a deformity, so HSA funds cannot be used for elective cosmetic work anywhere; they can be used for medically necessary care such as dental implants or bariatric surgery abroad.

pricesNote: US figures are ASPS average surgeon fees only (anesthesia, facility and tests extra) unless marked as marketplace ranges. Colombian clinic-published price lists are rare; the COP ranges below come from a Medellín-based reference list (April 2026, SCCP-certified surgeons in licensed clinics, converted at 4,150 COP per US dollar as that source did) and the US-dollar ranges from medical-tourism marketplaces, which are sales channels and are labelled as such. Marketplace Colombian prices typically exclude pre-op tests, hospitalization nights, garments, lymphatic massage, medication and the recovery house; budget 15% to 20% on top. Prices in Bogotá run about 5% above Medellín, Cali about 5% below. Get every inclusion in writing before paying a deposit.

process.title: First contact and the virtual consult
process.body: Most clinics and all coordinators start on WhatsApp or Instagram. Insist on a video consultation with the named surgeon, not a sales representative, and send your medical history, medications, BMI and photos. Bogotá's health secretariat said after the July 2026 death that 'lo barato no es seguro' and that patients must verify the facility and the professional before anything else.

process.title: Verify before you pay a deposit
process.body: Run the three lookups: the operating site in REPS (service 'cirugía plástica y estética' plus a licensed operating room), the surgeon in ReTHUS (specialty recorded, no sanctions) and the SCCP directory. Ask which hospital will take you if you deteriorate and whether an anesthesiologist, not the surgeon, gives anesthesia. Supersalud's own advice to foreign patients is to confirm habilitación and specialist status before any aesthetic procedure.

process.title: Quote, inclusions and refusal of 'combos'
process.body: Get an itemised written quote: surgeon, anesthesia, operating room, implants, nights in clinic, pre-op labs and EKG, garments, drains, lymphatic massages, medication, recovery house, transport and the follow-up visits. Cali's health secretary, the SCCP and Centro Médico Imbanaco have all warned against multi-procedure 'combos' in one anesthetic because risk rises with time under anesthesia; several foreign deaths in Cali followed three-procedure packages.

process.title: Arrival and pre-operative clearance
process.body: Plan to arrive 2 to 3 days before surgery for in-person labs, EKG, anesthesia assessment and a surgeon exam. A clinic that will operate the day you land is a red flag. CDC advises a travel-medicine visit 4 to 6 weeks before departure and up-to-date hepatitis B vaccination.

process.title: Surgery day
process.body: Confirm the surgery happens at the REPS-listed site, with an anesthesiologist present and an overnight stay for body contouring. In the 2025 Cali death of Alicia Stone the clinic was later closed temporarily for a staffing deficiency; in the 2021 Medellín death of a New York resident the patient removed his own drains in a hotel. Ask who monitors you the first night and where.

process.title: Recovery house or hotel
process.body: Recovery lodging is not regulated as a health service; the Personería de Medellín flagged soiled linen handling and unqualified staff in 2021. Prefer a clinic-run recovery unit or a hotel within minutes of a hospital emergency room, confirm who the on-call nurse is and how the surgeon is reached at night. Do not tour, drink or sunbathe during recovery.

process.title: Follow-up visits and the fly-home check
process.body: Expect drain removal and wound checks at 3 to 7 days. CDC guidance: no flying for 10 days after abdominal or chest surgery and 7 to 10 days after facial procedures. Before leaving, obtain the full operative report, anesthesia record, implant cards and pathology in English and Spanish.

process.title: Back home
process.body: Line up a US surgeon or primary-care clinician before you travel and tell them exactly what was done. CDC asks US clinicians to suspect nontuberculous mycobacteria in any post-travel surgical infection and to notify health departments; infections from these organisms often surface weeks later and need months of antibiotics. Revision surgery is at your own cost.

results.title: BBL carries the highest known cosmetic-surgery mortality
results.body: ASPS reports that early survey data put gluteal fat grafting deaths as high as 1 in 3,000, with later surveys closer to 1 in 15,000, about the rate for a tummy tuck. The cause is fat embolism when fat enters gluteal veins; the safety rule is subcutaneous injection only, never into the muscle. Ask the surgeon in writing how they inject.

results.title: Infections, especially mycobacteria, are the main documented harm
results.body: The CDC's 2026 review of US residents harmed after travel for cosmetic procedures found postsurgical infection in 20 of 21 consultations and suspected or confirmed nontuberculous mycobacteria in 12; four consultations involved deaths. In Medellín a single clandestine operator infected 40 of 55 women with a nontuberculous bacterium between 2023 and 2024, leaving permanent deformities.

results.title: Combined procedures and short trips raise risk
results.body: Cali's health secretary linked several foreign deaths to patients who arrived with little time and 'almost imposed' several procedures in one operation, because complication and death risk rise with anesthesia time. The ASPS Australia statement advises against combining surgery with a holiday because recovery needs rest and medical access that resort travel does not provide.

results.title: Revisions and complications are the patient's problem
results.body: ASPS notes that complications after medical tourism are most often paid for by Medicaid, that revision surgery is the patient's responsibility, and that suing a foreign surgeon in the US is rarely possible. For bariatric patients, ASMBS defines medical tourism as travel that precludes routine follow-up and says non-emergency follow-up of patients operated elsewhere is at the local surgeon's discretion, so secure a US program first.

safety.verdict: Colombia's accredited hospitals are a different world from its price-driven cosmetic market. The documented deaths of US and other foreign patients since 2016 cluster in Cali and Medellín cosmetic clinics, several of them licensed, usually after liposuction, fat grafting or multi-procedure 'combos', and Colombia keeps no national count. Add a Level 3 State Department advisory, repeated US Embassy alerts about drugging and dating-app robberies in Medellín, and an unregulated recovery-house trade, and the honest summary is: verifiable, licensed, single-procedure surgery with a registered plastic surgeon at a facility with a real operating room is reasonable; cheap packages are not.

points.title: Documented deaths of US patients
points.body: Alicia Stone, 40, an NYPD detective, died 23 October 2025 at Fundación Valle del Lili in Cali a week after liposuction and gluteal fat grafting at Plastikos Cirujanos S.A.S.; Cali's health secretariat temporarily closed the clinic for a staffing deficiency and the Fiscalía opened a negligence inquiry. Adriana Leon, 21, of West Springfield, Virginia, died in January 2020 at a post-op facility after skin-removal surgery; the surgeon's lawyer said the physician was never told of her complications. Jessica Joan Captorricio, 32, died in Cali in May 2018 after three procedures in one operation at a licensed clinic. Cristine Ann Deras, 28, of Florida, died in Cali in May 2017 after liposculpture, breast surgery and body contouring in one session. Diana Marcela Álvarez, 36, of Atlanta, died in Medellín in December 2016 at Clínica Arte y Cuerpo under a surgeon the ethics tribunal had suspended earlier that year. Mónica María Rodríguez, 52, a Colombian living in the US, died in Medellín in October 2022 after fat transfer at Interquirófanos in El Poblado.

points.title: Other foreign deaths and the pattern behind them
points.body: Alexánder Antonio Ramos, 40, a Dominican living in New York, died in Medellín in October 2021 after liposuction at Clínica de Especialistas de Antioquia; he had removed his drains in a hotel. Beatriz Adriana Maya López, a Mexican tourist, died in July 2023 at Clínica Las Vegas after a procedure in the south of the Aburrá valley. A 67-year-old Mexican man died in El Poblado in January 2025 during three facial procedures at a centre he found on TikTok. Elizabeth Sosa Sánchez, a Mexican engineer, died in Cali in August 2019 after a lipectomy, liposuction and gluteoplasty combo at a clinic that held permits. Evelin Durán, 50, of the Dominican Republic, died in 2018 after two operations in under 15 days. The recurring features are combined procedures, hotel recovery and clinics reached through social media.

points.title: Medellín and Antioquia's own counts
points.body: Antioquia's health secretary reported 11 deaths after cosmetic procedures in Medellín in 2024, five in 2025 and one in 2026 to May (Carolina Merchán Jaramillo, 30, after abdominoplasty with liposuction in El Poblado), plus 379 complications over two years and 64 aesthetic centres closed out of 80 inspected. Earlier reports put 2024 at 13 deaths in Antioquia, 10 in Medellín, with 125 complication cases to October. In 2023 five people died in the Aburrá valley, two of them foreigners. Clandestine 'clínicas de garaje' in Belén and La América advertise prices up to 70% below licensed centres; Bello alone closed more than 20 aesthetic centres in 2026.

points.title: Cali and Bogotá enforcement
points.body: Cali recorded 11 cosmetic-surgery deaths in 2017 and three by May 2018; the Valle del Cauca secretariat said it had closed 89 establishments in two years. Bogotá's health secretariat carried out 1,296 inspections of aesthetic businesses, 590 operations and 155 security measures between 2025 and July 2026; in May 2026 Supersalud shut the plastic-surgery service of Clínica de Obesidad y Envejecimiento and placed Clínica Láser Surgical under precautionary measures, and in July 2026 raids found foreign patients' passports at sites injecting banned biopolymers sold as 'stem cells'.

points.title: Licensed does not mean safe, and most of the dead were adults who did check
points.body: Several fatal clinics in Cali held permits; Cali's secretary said in 2017 that four of the clinics where patients died were licensed. The Alicia Stone clinic was licensed and was only closed afterwards. Licensing is necessary, not sufficient: the differentiators in the record are single procedures, a registered plastic surgeon, an anesthesiologist, overnight monitoring and a hospital within minutes.

points.title: US public-health evidence
points.body: CDC's June 2026 study of travel-related cosmetic procedures (2014 to 2024) found about 145 affected US residents in 21 consultations, nontuberculous mycobacteria in 12 of 20 infection clusters and deaths in four consultations; it does not name Colombia specifically. CDC's Yellow Book lists bloodstream and surgical-site infection, hepatitis B and C, antimicrobial-resistant organisms, clots, fat embolism and death among the risks and tells travelers to carry English records home.

points.title: Travel security: Level 3 advisory, drugging and dating-app robberies
points.body: The State Department rates Colombia Level 3, Reconsider Travel (updated 31 March 2026) for crime, terrorism, unrest and kidnapping, with Level 4 Do Not Travel for Arauca, Cauca except Popayán, Valle del Cauca except Cali, Norte de Santander and within 10 km of the Venezuelan border. The US Embassy warned on 10 January 2024 of eight suspicious deaths of US citizens in Medellín in November to December 2023, several tied to dating apps and sedative drugging, and issued a further 'Straight Talk About Crime' alert on 22 July 2026. Medellín's security data system recorded 428 drugging robberies in 2026 to August against 227 in all of 2025, led by El Poblado and Laureles, the two neighbourhoods where most cosmetic clinics and recovery houses are. Medellín authorities were investigating 17 foreigner deaths in 2025 to July.

points.title: What happens when complications surface in the US
points.body: ASPS says complications after surgery abroad are most often paid by Medicaid, revision is the patient's responsibility, and winning a judgment against a foreign surgeon in a US court is rarely possible. CDC asks US clinicians to notify health departments of medical-tourism complications. Your Colombian recourse is a Supersalud complaint, a health-secretariat report and the Fiscalía, none of which pays for your care.

redFlags: The surgeon does not appear in ReTHUS with 'cirugía plástica, estética y reconstructiva' as a registered specialty, or appears only as a general physician, dentist or 'médico estético'.
The operating site is not in REPS, or is licensed only for outpatient consultation, dermatology or 'medicina estética' with no surgical service and no operating room listed.
You were recruited through Instagram, TikTok or WhatsApp by a 'coordinator' who takes payment and will not name the clinic and surgeon in writing.
A 'combo' of three or more procedures (for example liposuction, tummy tuck and BBL) is offered in one anesthetic, or two surgeries within two weeks.
Surgery is scheduled the day you land, with no in-person labs, EKG or anesthesiology assessment.
Anesthesia is given by the surgeon or a nurse, not a named anesthesiologist, or the clinic cannot say which hospital receives emergencies.
Recovery is in an apartment, Airbnb or hotel with no nurse, or the clinic sends you to a 'recovery house' it will not name in the contract.
The price is far below the reference ranges (for example liposuction under about US$1,900 or BBL under about US$2,900) or is 70% below licensed clinics in the same city.

Injectables sold as 'stem cells', 'fat burners', 'biopolymers' or 'hydrogel' for buttocks or body contouring; biopolymers are banned by Ley 2316 de 2023 and Supersalud has found 'stem cell' offers that were biopolymers.
The clinic or coordinator discourages you from telling your US doctor, refuses to provide English records, or asks you to sign a waiver of the right to complain or sue.

entry.title: Entry and visa rules for US citizens (October 2026)
entry.body: US citizens enter visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days at the immigration officer's discretion, extendable through Migración Colombia up to 180 days in any 12-month period. Carry a passport valid for your stay (Colombian immigration recommends six months beyond departure) and proof of an onward or return ticket. Migración Colombia's CheckMig online pre-registration can be completed from 72 hours to one hour before each flight in and out; the UK government describes it as optional but it speeds entry and airlines may ask for the confirmation. Yellow-fever certificates are required only if arriving from certain countries. Expect a spot interview; say truthfully that you are coming for medical treatment and bring your clinic appointment letter.

flights.title: Flights and typical fares
flights.body: Miami has nonstop service to Bogotá, Medellín, Cali, Barranquilla and Cartagena on American, Avianca, LATAM and others; New York (JFK and Newark) has nonstops to Bogotá and Medellín. Nonstop Miami to Cali or Medellín round trips were advertised around US$386 to US$391 in 2026 deal listings and American showed Miami to Cali from US$315 and Miami to Medellín from US$378 on specific dates; a 2026 marketplace guide budgets US$400 to US$800 round trip. Flight time from Miami is about three and a half hours to Bogotá. Book a changeable return: CDC advises no flying for 10 days after abdominal or chest surgery and 7 to 10 days after facial work, and complications push that out.

whereToStay.title: Where to stay
whereToStay.body: Cosmetic clinics cluster in El Poblado and Laureles (Medellín), the north and Tequendama sectors of Cali, and Chapinero and Usaquén (Bogotá). El Poblado and Laureles also recorded the most drugging robberies in Medellín in 2026 (108 and 106 cases to August) and are where the US Embassy's dating-app warnings apply. Choose a hotel or clinic-run recovery unit within minutes of a hospital emergency room, with a front desk that registers visitors by physical cédula, and avoid short-term rentals for the first nights after surgery. Recovery houses are not licensed health providers; the Personería de Medellín has flagged hygiene and staffing gaps.

payment.title: Paying
payment.body: Pay the licensed clinic (the REPS-registered legal entity) directly by card or bank transfer and get an invoice in its name; do not wire money to a coordinator's personal account. Deposits of 10% to 30% are common; refuse to pay the balance in cash on arrival without a receipt. Elective cosmetic surgery is not an HSA-eligible or deductible expense under IRS Publication 502 unless it corrects a deformity; medically necessary care abroad (dental implants, bariatric or orthopedic surgery) is treated like domestic care for deduction purposes, subject to the 7.5% of adjusted gross income floor. US health plans generally exclude cosmetic surgery and its complications. Budget 15% to 20% above the quote for extras.

stayAndFlyHome.title: How long to stay and when you can fly
stayAndFlyHome.body: CDC: do not fly for 10 days after chest or abdominal surgery (liposuction of the trunk, tummy tuck, BBL, breast surgery, bariatric and cardiac procedures) and wait 7 to 10 days after laser or cosmetic procedures of the face, eyelids or nose. Joint replacement patients typically stay two to three weeks and need clearance for clot risk. Dental implant patients can usually fly within days but must return for crowns months later. Build in time for drain removal, a final surgeon visit and collection of records, and buy a changeable ticket.

aftercareAtHome.title: Aftercare in the US
aftercareAtHome.body: Arrange a US plastic surgeon, bariatric program or dentist willing to see you before you leave, because ASMBS says follow-up of patients operated elsewhere is at the local surgeon's discretion and ASPS warns revision is your cost. Bring English operative notes, anesthesia records, implant cards and antibiotic names. Seek care immediately for fever, redness, drainage or nodules at incision sites even weeks later, and tell clinicians about the trip; CDC flags nontuberculous mycobacteria as the pathogen to suspect and asks clinicians to notify health departments.

booking.title: Decide the procedure and the city before the clinic
booking.body: Cosmetic surgery: Cali, Medellín, Bogotá. Dental: Bogotá, Medellín, Cali. Cardiac, orthopedic, oncology: the accredited hospitals in Bogotá, Medellín and Cali. Keep it to one procedure per anesthetic.

booking.title: Shortlist surgeons from the SCCP directory, not from Instagram
booking.body: Start at cirugiaplastica.org.co/buscar-cirujano, then confirm each name in ReTHUS and find the clinic they operate at in REPS. For hospitals, check Icontec's accredited list and JCI's directory.

booking.title: Video consult with the surgeon
booking.body: Ask about board certification and ReTHUS registration, how many of this exact procedure they do a year, where you will be operated and by whom anesthesia is given, their complication plan and receiving hospital, and for BBL whether they inject subcutaneously only.

booking.title: Written itemised quote
booking.body: Get surgeon, anesthesia, facility, implants, nights, labs, garments, massages, medication, recovery lodging, transport and follow-ups itemised, with the cancellation and complication policy, and in the clinic's legal name.

booking.title: Pre-travel medical prep in the US
booking.body: See your primary-care clinician and a travel-medicine clinic 4 to 6 weeks out, update hepatitis B, stop blood thinners and supplements as instructed, enrol in the State Department's STEP program and buy travel insurance with medical evacuation. Check whether your policy excludes elective surgery abroad.

booking.title: Book flights, lodging and a companion
booking.body: Arrive 2 to 3 days early, book a changeable return at least 10 to 14 days after body surgery, and bring a companion; several fatal cases involved patients alone in hotels after surgery.

booking.title: Complete CheckMig and arrival logistics
booking.body: Fill in CheckMig 72 to 1 hours before each flight, use the clinic's or hotel's named driver, and do not use dating apps or accept drinks from strangers during recovery, per US Embassy alerts.

booking.title: Keep records and know where to complain
booking.body: Leave with full records in English. If something goes wrong, report to the city health secretariat, file a PQRD with Supersalud through SuperArgo, and if there is harm, file with the Fiscalía; keep every receipt and message.

vetChecklist: Screenshot of the REPS entry for the exact operating site showing 'cirugía plástica y estética' (or the relevant surgical service) and a licensed operating room under installed capacity.
Screenshot of the surgeon's ReTHUS record showing the surgical specialty and no sanctions, matched to the cédula number on the consent form.
The surgeon's SCCP membership (or equivalent specialty society for non-plastic procedures) and the university that granted the specialty title.
Name and ReTHUS record of the anesthesiologist who will be present for the whole operation.
The name of the receiving hospital for emergencies, in writing, and its distance from the clinic and from your lodging.
An itemised quote in the clinic's legal name listing every inclusion and exclusion, the cancellation policy and who pays for treating complications.
Written confirmation that only one procedure (or a stated, limited combination) will be done, with the planned anesthesia time.
For implants or grafts: brand, model and serial numbers and that you will receive the implant card; for BBL, written confirmation of subcutaneous-only injection.
The recovery lodging's name, address, on-site nursing arrangement and night contact for the surgeon.
A commitment to provide the operative report, anesthesia record, pathology and discharge instructions in English before you fly, and the date of your last in-person check.

faqs.question: How many Americans actually go to Colombia for medical care?
faqs.answer: Colombia recorded 26,786 non-resident foreigners entering for health reasons in 2025, and Anato puts the US at about 41% of health visitors, so roughly 11,000 Americans a year by that measure. Migración Colombia counts self-declared motives, so the true number is higher.

faqs.question: Is plastic surgery in Colombia safe?
faqs.answer: Not as a category. Antioquia's health secretary counted 11 cosmetic-procedure deaths in Medellín in 2024, five in 2025 and one by May 2026, and foreign patients, including an NYPD detective in Cali in October 2025, are among the dead. Risk drops sharply with a ReTHUS-registered plastic surgeon, a REPS-licensed operating room, an anesthesiologist and one procedure at a time.

faqs.question: How do I check a Colombian surgeon's licence?
faqs.answer: Search the SISPRO ReTHUS page by name or cédula; it shows profession, registered specialty, authorizing entity and sanctions. The Ministry says practicing a surgical specialty not recorded in ReTHUS is illegal. Then confirm membership at the SCCP's 'Buscar Cirujano' directory.

faqs.question: How do I check whether a clinic is licensed?
faqs.answer: Use REPS at prestadores.minsalud.gov.co/habilitacion: open 'Registro Actual', search the provider, then check 'Servicios' for 'cirugía plástica y estética' and 'Capacidad instalada' for an operating room at the exact site. A clinic licensed only for consultations may not operate.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a plastic surgeon and a 'cirujano estético'?
faqs.answer: Colombia recognises one specialty, cirugía plástica, estética y reconstructiva, which requires a postgraduate surgical residency. 'Medicina estética' and 'cirugía estética' are not recognised specialties and are often taught in short courses. General physicians and non-doctors have performed liposuction and gluteal injections in several fatal cases.

faqs.question: How much does a BBL or liposuction cost in Colombia versus the US?
faqs.answer: A Medellín reference list puts liposuction at COP 8 to 18 million (about US$1,900 to 4,300) and BBL at COP 12 to 25 million (about US$2,900 to 6,000) with surgeon, anesthesia and operating room included. ASPS average US surgeon fees alone are US$4,711 for liposuction and US$7,264 for fat-graft buttock augmentation.

faqs.question: Why are 'combo' packages dangerous?
faqs.answer: Cali's health secretary, the SCCP and Centro Médico Imbanaco have warned that risk of complications and death rises with time under anesthesia, and several foreign deaths in Cali followed three procedures in one operation. Ask for one procedure per anesthetic and at least several weeks between surgeries.

faqs.question: Are stem cell treatments in Medellín legal and approved?
faqs.answer: They are not FDA approved, and Colombia has no general authorization for stem cell therapy outside clinical trials and established blood-disorder uses. INVIMA has approved specific trials, and in 2026 Supersalud found 'stem cell' offers in Bogotá that were actually banned biopolymers. Treat them as experimental.

faqs.question: Can I use my HSA or deduct the cost?
faqs.answer: Elective cosmetic surgery is not a qualified medical expense under IRS Publication 502 unless it corrects a deformity, in Colombia or anywhere. Medically necessary care abroad, such as dental implants or bariatric surgery, is treated like domestic care for the deduction (above 7.5% of adjusted gross income) and HSA purposes.

faqs.question: Will my US insurance cover complications?
faqs.answer: Generally no for cosmetic surgery and its complications; ASPS notes that most plans exclude them and that complications after surgery abroad are often paid by Medicaid or the patient. Emergency care at a US hospital will still be provided, but revision surgery is at your cost.

faqs.question: When can I fly home after surgery?
faqs.answer: CDC advises no flying for 10 days after chest or abdominal surgery, which covers liposuction of the trunk, tummy tuck, BBL, breast and bariatric surgery, and waiting 7 to 10 days after facial, eyelid or nose procedures. Buy a changeable ticket.

faqs.question: Is Medellín safe for a solo medical traveler?
faqs.answer: The State Department rates Colombia Level 3, Reconsider Travel, and the US Embassy has issued alerts in January 2024 and July 2026 about drugging and robbery of foreigners met through dating apps. Medellín logged 428 drugging robberies in 2026 to August, most in El Poblado and Laureles. Bring a companion, skip dating apps, and use clinic drivers.

faqs.question: Which parts of Colombia does the US say not to visit?
faqs.answer: As of the 31 March 2026 advisory: Arauca, Cauca except Popayán, Valle del Cauca except Cali, Norte de Santander and within 10 km of the Venezuelan border are Level 4, Do Not Travel. Bogotá, Medellín, Cali, Barranquilla and Cartagena are not excluded but fall under the national Level 3.

faqs.question: What can I do if something goes wrong in Colombia?
faqs.answer: Report the clinic to the city health secretariat, which can inspect and seal it; file a free PQRD complaint with Supersalud through the SuperArgo portal; and file a criminal complaint with the Fiscalía if there was harm. Civil damages need a Colombian lawyer; US courts rarely have jurisdiction.

faqs.question: Do I need a visa or any form to enter Colombia?
faqs.answer: US citizens enter visa-free for up to 90 days with a passport valid for the stay and an onward ticket. Migración Colombia's CheckMig pre-registration can be completed 72 to 1 hours before each flight; it speeds entry and some airlines request it.
